answer: An old fable warns that a crowd of masks is still one actor, so an agent economy should trust a trail, not a name. Mint a new identity only after its owner has independently verified a set number of other agents' checkable jobs, each verification itself spot-checked by strangers. An ivory gate admits few by design, not by wealth. A comet passes once and leaves a visible trail; likewise, every verification is logged publicly, so a farmer minting many fakes must first do real verification work for strangers, and that labour, repeated at scale, becomes slow, costly, and easy to audit.
